summary: Daisy Cheung specializes in Indology and Tibetology. She earned an MArch (2005) and MBS (2011) at the University of Hong Kong and a PhD from the University of Hamburg (2021). She became a postdoctoral research fellow at the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 2024.

Daito Shimaji (1875–1927) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University and Otani University, and later taught at Komazawa, Rissho, Toyo (~1904–1927), and the University of Tokyo (1923).

Dale S. Wright is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Alan Anderson, Wang Pachow, and Robert P. Scharlemann, and served as David B. and Mary H. Gamble Professor at Occidental College from around 1980.

Dalpat Rajpurohit specializes in Indology. He earned a BA from Jai Narain Vyas University, an MPhil from Jawaharlal Nehru University, and a PhD from Presidency University. He lectured at Columbia University (2008–2018) before becoming assistant professor at UT Austin in 2019.

Dalsukh Malvania (1910–2000) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1948–1959), L.D. Institute of Indology as director (~1963–1978), the Prakrit Text Society (1962), and the University of Toronto.
Damaru Chandra Bhatta works in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Tribhuvan University and served as an associate professor at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus in 1994.
Damchö Gyatso is a scholar who studied under Penor Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche.
Damdin Badaraev is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who studied under Bidia Dandaron and George de Roerich.

Damien Keown is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Lancaster University and the University of Oxford, he served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Ethics at Goldsmiths, University of London, and co-founded the Journal of Buddhist Ethics in 1994.
Damodar was an Indology scholar who served as Head Pandit at Maharaja's High School, Srinagar, and at Maharaja's Pathashala (attested 1892).

Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi (1907–1966) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Harvard under George David Birkhoff and held posts at Banaras Hindu University, Aligarh Muslim University, Fergusson College, the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (1945–1962), and CSIR (1964).

Dan Arnold is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at Carleton College, Columbia, Iliff, and the University of Chicago, he held faculty posts at McGill University (2003–2004) and the University of Chicago (2004–2011).
Dan Li specializes in linguistics and Buddhist studies. Having studied under Sherab Gyatso, Li held an associate professor post at Soka University (attested 2026).

Dan Lusthaus specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a PhD from Temple University and held posts at Bates College, Grinnell College (1988–1989), Florida State University (attested 1996–1999), University of Georgia (attested 2000), and Harvard University (2005).

Dan Martin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ohio State, Kent State, and Indiana University under Elliot Sperling, later holding posts at the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters, Hebrew University, and Swarthmore College.

Dan Smyer Yü works in religious studies and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from the University of California, Davis, and served as a research group leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

Dan Zahavi is a philosopher who studied at KU Leuven under Rudolf Bernet and the University of Copenhagen. He has served as a professor at the University of Copenhagen since 2002 and held a post at the University of Oxford (2018–2021).

Daniel Aaron Getz works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a PhD from Yale University under Stanley Weinstein, also studying under Ying-shih Yü and Tairyo Makita, and served as an associate professor at Bradley University (attested 2019).
Daniel Amadé Scheidegger is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed a doctoral degree at the University of Bristol under supervisor Paul Williams.

Daniel B. Stevenson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. After earning a PhD from Columbia University, he held assistant professor positions at Butler University (attested 1986) and the University of Kansas (attested 1996–2003).
